relevance.rationale: BROKEN SOURCE JOIN: the named file does not exist; the real source is library/arxiv-1007.1250v4/1007.1250v4.pdf, already a separate unreviewed ledger row. Identity unconfirmable here. KEY-OVERLOAD DEFECT, the largest citation-hygiene finding in this slice: this single id is cited across the Lean tree with SIX mutually incompatible DOIs (only one of which matches the registered entry; the strings are enumerated in the triage summary). The distinct-DOI sites are brings-surface/local-cohomology-group.lean:17, brings-surface/topological-charge-quantization.lean:15 and :38, quantum-observable-universes/rigid-dualizing-complex.lean:45/52/60, information-theory/mass-energy-equivalence.lean:21 and :58, information-theory/quantum-entropy.lean:39 and :47, mass-theory/knot-factor-frobenius-pairing.lean:32, quantum-observable-universes/substrate-self-duality.lean:71, and mass-theory/tau-all-orders-bridge.lean:7 (bare arXiv id). One id cannot be six different works. MISCITED CLAIM: quantum-observable-universes/rigid-dualizing-complex.lean:51-52 cites this id at 'Theorem 4.2' for the full construction of a RIGID DUALIZING COMPLEX. That is not the subject of the work the id names (nonabelian multiplicative integration on surfaces); rigid dualizing complexes are a separate line of work by the same author. quantum-entropy.lean:39/47 likewise attaches a monograph-series DOI unrelated to the registered one. By contrast the nonabelian-Stokes uses are on-topic and read as load-bearing: mass-endomorphism/mass-identity-C-proof.md:4 and :19, mass-endomorphism/topological-mass-holonomy-proof.md:24, lifting-and-descent/descent-physical.md:4, mass-endomorphism/mass-identity-C.md:1.

proposedActions.rationale: The rigid-dualizing-complex citation is the clearest wrong-source case: a Theorem 4.2 about rigid dualizing complexes is attributed to a work on nonabelian multiplicative integration. Record the discrepancy and split the overloaded id before any further block cites it.

relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED against the document's front matter — and this is the most heavily cited reference in the slice (~90 sites), genuinely core to the mass-identity chain. But it carries THREE defects, two of them claim-level. (1) MISCITED SOURCE — `rigid-dualizing-complex.lean`. Lines 45, 51, 52 and 60 cite this id — three of them naming 'Theorem 4.2' — for the EXISTENCE OF A RIGID DUALIZING COMPLEX and Van den Bergh duality. `grep -i dualizing` over the full extracted text of this document returns ZERO hits. The document is differential geometry (Lie crossed modules, kites, nonabelian Stokes); rigid dualizing complexes belong to a different research line by the same author. The theorem being invoked is not in this document. Corroborating signal: those same lines carry an identifier that is NOT the one registered for this key and that resolves to a book by that author, i.e. the site is pointing at a different work which has no `ref()` entry of its own. Note also that `rigid_dualizing_exists` is discharged by an explicitly trivial witness ('all Prop fields = True'), so the citation is doing the rhetorical work of suggesting a real theorem behind a vacuous proof. (2) WRONG LOCATOR — `topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp-proof.md:38` cites '[Proposition 5.3, yekutieli2015]' for 'additivity of the nonabelian multiplicative integral over orthogonal direct sums'. The document has no Proposition 5.3; it has Proposition 5.3.3 (three-level numbering), which concerns a Lie quasi crossed module with additive feedback and its connection–curvature pairs — not additivity over orthogonal direct sums. Scope-(a): as read, the document does not supply that statement at that locator. (3) SIX DIFFERENT IDENTIFIERS FOR ONE KEY across the 27 identifier-bearing citation sites: the registered one at 18 sites, and five others at 4, 2, 1, 1 and 1 sites respectively. Nine sites point somewhere other than the registered work. WHAT IS SOLID: the nonabelian-Stokes citations (`nonabelian_stokes_surface_boundary_stokes.lean`, `mass-identity-C.lean`, `topological-charge-quantization.lean`, `NonAbelianStokes.lean`) match the document's actual main results — the 2-dimensional nonabelian Stokes theorem generalising Schlesinger's, and the 3-dimensional nonabelian Stokes theorem its abstract calls 'a totally new result'.

keyResults.locator: Abstract; 2-d nonabelian Stokes theorem; 3-d nonabelian Stokes theorem
keyResults.statement: A twisted 2-dimensional nonabelian multiplicative integral over kites in a pointed manifold, valued in the second Lie group of a Lie crossed module, satisfying a 2-dimensional nonabelian Stokes theorem (generalising Schlesinger's) and a 3-dimensional nonabelian Stokes theorem.
keyResults.useForFolio: The genuine load-bearing content behind the mass-identity / holonomy chain; the citations that name Stokes are correct.

keyResults.locator: Prop. 5.3.3 (the only 5.3-prefixed result in the document)
keyResults.statement: For a Lie quasi crossed module with additive feedback over X, f*(α) and Lie(Θ_G)(α) relate as stated for connection–curvature pairs.
keyResults.useForFolio: Establishes that the cited 'Proposition 5.3' locator does not exist and that 5.3.3 is not an orthogonal-direct-sum additivity statement.

proposedActions.rationale: rigid-dualizing-complex.lean attributes a rigid-dualizing-complex existence theorem to a document that contains no dualizing-complex content. Either identify and register the correct source (the work the site's own identifier already points at) under its own key, or drop the attribution — the current state pairs a wrong citation with a trivially-witnessed theorem.
Correct or remove the '[Proposition 5.3, yekutieli2015]' locator; the document's numbering is three-level and 5.3.3 says something else.
Normalise the nine citation sites carrying one of the five non-registered identifiers, splitting off any that genuinely mean a different work of the same author into their own ref() entries.
